Fasting plasma glucose
In the late 1960s, it was generally acknowledged that the FPG test was suboptimal for the diabetes diagnosis. Before 1997, diabetes
was diagnosed based on FPG levels >7.8 mmol/L (140 mg/dL), arbitrarily determined to represent the upper threshold of normal
FPG. In 1997, the ADA Expert Committee revised the criteria by lowering the FPG cut-point from 7.8 mmol/L (140 mg/dL) to
7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL) and retained the 2 h PG value for the diagnosis of diabetes (Fig. 1). The revision of the FPG cut-point
